task_instance: Build a native-feeling Expo Settings screen (Expo Router app) following the skill's guidance: centralized theme/colors.ts using the `Color` API from expo-router for semantic iOS/Android colors, a grouped settings card using @expo/ui's `Toggle` (SwiftUI-backed control per the skill's library preference over React Native's Switch), SF Symbols via expo-symbols' SymbolView, ScrollView with contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior='automatic' for safe-area handling, CSS boxShadow instead of legacy shadow props, selectable Text, and borderCurve:'continuous' rounding. Verified by type-checking with tsc and bundling the app for iOS with `npx expo export`.
evidence: Scaffolded an Expo SDK 57 TypeScript app at MyApp/ (blank-typescript template). Installed expo-router, react-native-safe-area-context, react-native-screens, expo-symbols, expo-blur, @expo/ui via npm (plain `expo install` failed with 'HTTP Proxy Network Error: Forbidden' when it tried to reach the React Native Directory compatibility API at reactnative.directory - unrelated sandboxed network check, worked around by using plain `npm install --legacy-peer-deps`, which succeeded). Wrote MyApp/theme/colors.ts implementing the skill's exact Color/PlatformColor pattern (Platform.select wrapping Color.ios.* / Color.android.dynamic.* with hex fallbacks). Wrote MyApp/app/_layout.tsx (Stack) and MyApp/app/index.tsx: a Settings screen with a grouped card (secondarySystemBackground, borderRadius+borderCurve:'continuous', boxShadow), two rows each with an SF Symbol (SymbolView from expo-symbols) and an @expo/ui/swift-ui `Toggle` control (isOn/onIsOnChange - discovered via node_modules/@expo/ui/build/swift-ui d.ts files that the exported name is `Toggle`, not `Switch`, and corrected the code), wrapped in a ScrollView with contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior='automatic' and keyboardShouldPersistTaps='handled', plus a selectable footnote Text. Configured tsconfig.json path alias '@/*' and app.json ('scheme', 'plugins': ['expo-router'], userInterfaceStyle: 'automatic'). `npx tsc --noEmit` passed with zero errors. `npx expo export --platform ios` succeeded: Metro bundled 1210 modules into a 2.5MB Hermes bytecode bundle at MyApp/dist/_expo/static/js/ios/index-*.hbc alongside assets and metadata.json, confirming the screen and all native-UI imports (expo-router Color API, @expo/ui, expo-symbols, react-native-safe-area-context) resolve and compile correctly end-to-end. Running the bundle live in Expo Go on a physical/simulated device was out of scope for this sandbox (no device/simulator available), but the skill's core deliverable - producing a correct, native-styled Expo screen using its prescribed APIs and libraries that builds successfully - was fully achieved and verified via type-check + bundle export.
